title: A rate limit's available capacity is min(slope x elapsed time + last amount, maxAmount), with 'unlimited' encoded as a sentinel maximum
content:
A.6.1.1.3.2.6.1.2.2.1.1.3.4 gives the exact rule for `getCurrentRateLimit`: if `maxAmount` is `type(uint256).max` the contract returns that sentinel, "otherwise, the contract will calculate and return the minimum of (slope * time elapsed since lastUpdated + lastAmount) and maxAmount."

This is a continuous leaky bucket, not a periodic quota. Capacity begins refilling the instant after use, so there is no reset boundary to camp on — the exploit of draining a daily allowance at 23:59 and again at 00:01 does not exist here. A relayer that consumes the full limit must wait proportionally to the amount consumed, which is what turns `slope` into a genuine flow ceiling.

The `min(...)` is the invariant guard: accrued capacity can never exceed `maxAmount`, no matter how long the limit has gone unused. Idle time does not bank exposure.

The sentinel encoding is the other design choice worth keeping. "Unlimited" is not a separate flag or a bypass path but the extreme value of the same field, and `setUnlimitedRateLimitData` (…3.3) simply calls the normal setter with `type(uint256).max` and slope 0. `triggerRateLimitDecrease` (…3.5) then returns unchanged in that case. One code path serves both bounded and unbounded limits, so the unlimited case cannot diverge in behaviour from the limited one — which matters because the unbounded limits are exactly the emergency exits.
description: Capacity accrues linearly from the last use rather than resetting on a schedule, and the unlimited case is expressed as maxAmount = type(uint256).max with slope 0, short-circuiting the arithmetic.
